sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; unitary fiscal jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States DTA (1996, as amended 2004 and 2019)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement BEPS Tax Treaty Measures (MLI, applicable to Luxembourg DTAs)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (consolidated, as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing EU Directive 2018/843 and by the Law of 23 December 2022); Law of 13 January 2019 instituting the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended); Grand-Ducal Regulations and CSSF circulars on AML/CFT customer due diligence. RBE access is restricted by law to competent authorities and AML/CFT obliged entities; public access remains suspended following CJEU judgments C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or competent registry authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the Articles of Association (statuts) of each foreign corporate shareholder, with sworn translation into French, German or English
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public at the corporate shareholder's seat

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of each UBO, director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the UBO's country of residence or national passport issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's reference letter and KYC/FATCA-CRS self-certification evidencing source of funds of each shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depositary bank or independent financial institution of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for the bank's certificate) OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory at pre-incorporation: (i) full-chain UBO identification covering direct and indirect ownership of at least 25% plus control-by-other-means analysis; (ii) scheduled screening against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (FSDB), US OFAC SDN List, Luxembourg national sanctions list, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction advisories; (iii) PEP classification per the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02, including family members and close associates, triggering mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence; (iv) documented source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification; (v) negative-news and adverse-media assessment; (vi) issuance of a formal business risk rating (Low_Risk_Standard for ISIC 4791 online furniture retail) and commitment to post-incorporation transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCSL Portal, official registry service at www.lbr.lu (Sociétés et Organismes — réservation de dénomination)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in French, German, Luxembourgish, or any Latin-script language; an English name is acceptable for this e-commerce SARL provided the legal form designation 'SARL' is appended. Non-Latin script names require a sworn-translator-certified transliteration before RCSL submission. The name must be distinctive, non-misleading as to corporate activity, and free from identity or similarity conflict with any existing Luxembourg registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fund / Fonds / SICAV / SICAR / UCITS / Investment Fund / Organisme de Placement Collectif
State / État / Trésor / Commune / Municipal / National
Luxembourg / Letzeburg / Luxemburg (requires prior ministerial authorization or demonstrated legitimate interest)
European / International (requires demonstrable cross-border activity and prior approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection the applicant may: (1) immediately re-file an alternative name through the LBR online portal with a fresh statutory fee and no cooling-off period; (2) submit a reasoned written request to the RCSL legal service for administrative authorization of a sensitive or contested name; (3) lodge a formal administrative appeal before the Tribunal Administratif within three months of the refusal notification under the Law of 3 March 2020 on administrative justice, with further appellate review by the Cour Administrative; (4) if the notarial deed is not executed within the 30-day reservation window, a fresh name reservation application must be filed; the reservation fee is forfeited in all cases of rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as standalone substance: the SARL must maintain a domestic statutory seat and a physical operational anchor in Luxembourg. An approved domiciliation arrangement under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016, is permissible for this non-financial e-commerce activity provided the company retains a Luxembourg-based management function, documented decision-making records, and a functional communication channel. A purely remote virtual office with no physical anchor is rejected by the RCSL, the AEDT, and the ACD for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 30 to 40 percent within the first 24 months for cross-border e-commerce operators; unannounced physical inspections may be conducted by the Administration des Contributions Directes, the Administration de l'Enregistrement des Domaines et de la TVA, the FIU/Public Prosecutor's Office, and the RCSL to verify real presence, commercial substance, inventory/logistics arrangements, and the Luxembourg locus of management decisions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL Company Name Reservation and pre-due-diligence name search (réservation de dénomination)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per LBR fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for drafting and execution of the Acte Constitutif of the SARL (articles of association)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff for standard SARL with single or multi-shareholder structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL commercial register filing (immatriculation) and legal publication in the electronic company gazette (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory electronic filing fee; RESA publication free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) initial declaration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory e-filing fee for the beneficial owner declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance pack: full-chain UBO identification, PEP classification, UN/EU/OFAC/Luxembourg sanctions screening, and formal risk assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark at EUR 350 to EUR 450 per hour, fixed-fee pre-incorporation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of corporate and UBO documentation into French, German or English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted to the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice list
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document sworn translation tariff according to language pair and complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or Consular Legalization processing of foreign shareholder and UBO documentation bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home-country competent authority or Luxembourg consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille fee schedule or consular legalization tariff per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / approved domiciliation agreement for the SARL (annual service under the Law of 31 May 1999)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved domiciliation agent registered with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market benchmark for a non-financial e-commerce SARL with standard substance profile

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation bank KYC dossier and CRS/FATCA self-certification preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate secretarial firm or Luxembourg tax advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a Low_Risk_Standard banking AML risk tier dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for notarial disbursements, registry variances and international courier of apostilled documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Safety buffer of approximately 7 percent of total pre-incorporation budget

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended; SARL-specific provisions at Articles 180-1 through 180-33; incorporation formalities and publicity at Articles 1, 9, 10, 12 and 1600-1; RCS registration and RESA publication governed by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 21, rue de Luxembourg, L-8077 Bertrange; e-filing mandatory via the e-RCS single online portal (www.lbr.lu).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized articles of association (statuts constitutifs) executed before a Luxembourg notary, accompanied by the RCS registration application (demande d'inscription au RCS) and certified extract transmitted for publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 1 is permitted under the reformed 2016/2017 SARL regime; capital must be fully subscribed at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution, and a banker's release certificate (attestation de blocage) is required by the notary. In commercial practice, capital of at least EUR 12,000 is set to facilitate bank KYC and trade credit; contributions in kind require an independent auditor's valuation report (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD/INITIAL SHAREHOLDERS OF [●] S.À R.L. — Whereas the articles of association were subscribed before Notary [●] on [date], and the initial share capital of EUR [●] has been fully subscribed and deposited with [Bank]; IT IS RESOLVED: (1) to ratify the incorporation act and confirm share allocation as listed in the statutes; (2) to adopt the registered office at [●], Luxembourg; (3) to appoint [Name] as manager (gérant), with sole signature authority; (4) to approve and file incorporation with the RCS/LBR and arrange RESA publication; (5) to open bank and payment accounts; (6) to cause VAT, CIT, municipal business tax and social security registrations; and (7) to empower the manager to execute all carrying-out documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-filing name approval and structural lock (RCS negative certificate and articles drafting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) via the e-RCS portal; notary of the registered office district
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the corporate name and obtain a negative certificate (certificat négatif) confirming the name is available; coordinate with the chosen Luxembourg notary to draft the statuts covering share capital, share classes, number of managers, and corporate objects limited to online retail of oversized furniture and home decor under ISIC 4791 with no regulated banking or financial activity; schedule a notarization date as soon as the certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Certificat négatif de la dénomination socio (name reservation receipt)
Draft articles of association (statuts)
Identity documents/passport copies of each shareholder and manager
Proof of registered office availability (lease, ownership title or domiciliation agreement)
Internal business plan and capital structure memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged by the RCS, apply for an alternative name and amend the draft statutes; an RCS query letter (observation) must be answered by the notary within 1 month, otherwise the file is closed and must be re-submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital escrow and banker's release certificate at a Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed bank (e.g., BIL, Spuerkeess, ING Luxembourg) selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary 'blocked account' in the name of the company in formation ('[●] SARL en formation') and deposit the full subscribed cash capital; the bank issues a release/blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) to be annexed to the notarial deed; perform full KYC/AML identification of the beneficial owners in accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CFT, as amended, and the CSSF circulars.
required_dossiers: Corporate KYC/AML file of each shareholder (identity, source of funds, tax residence)
Copy of the draft statuts or a signed side letter of intention
Evidence of capital funds and bank reference letters
Beneficial ownership declaration for the RCS register (post-incorporation filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC documentation, provide certified translations and additional source-of-wealth evidence; any delay in the bank certificate postpones the notarial deed — re-schedule the notary date once the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary appointed within the Luxembourg-Mersch judicial district (acte constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders or their notarized attorneys-in-fact appear before the notary, declare subscription of the entire share capital, adopt the statuts, and sign the deed; the notary collects the banker's release certificate, verifies legal capacity and identity of signatories, checks conformity of the corporate object with Luxembourg law and public policy, and issues an authentic instrument for registration.
required_dossiers: Valid passports/IDs of all founders and managers
Executed attorney powers (procurations) if a founder is not appearing personally
Banker's certificate of capital deposit (attestation de blocage)
Certificat négatif for the name as issued by LBR
Evidence of registered office address (lease or domiciliation contract)
Declaration of non-conviction and management eligibility statements of the appointed manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a defect (missing translations, unauthorized corporate purpose, prohibited share structure), the deficit is cured via an addendum (avenant) or re-notarization; the deed is not signed until all attachments are complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and RESA publication (acquisition of legal personality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR); RESA (electronic gazette of companies and associations) under the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the deed to the RCS within 15 days of signature via the e-RCS portal; the RCS verifies name availability, statutory conformity and attachments, allocates the registration number (immatriculation number / numéro d'immatriculation), registers the company, and publication in the RESA follows within one business day; legal personality becomes fully effective upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized original deed with RCS registration form (formulaire d'inscription au RCS)
Certified list of managers (gérants) indicating signature powers
Banker's release certificate annexed to the deed
Registry fees receipt (droit de dépôt)
Beneficial ownership information for the RCS beneficial-owner register (if requested at filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a completeness request, the notary/applicant must cure within the provided deadline (usually 1–2 months); refusals can be appealed to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within 15 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration with ACD, AEDT and CCSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD — income tax), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT — registration duties and VAT), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SARL for corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT) by filing the formation forms with ACD; apply to AEDT for the VAT number (LUX + 8 digits) using the VAT registration form; register the manager(s) and any employees with CCSS for social security; in parallel, file the beneficial-owner declaration (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) at RCS/LBR within one month of incorporation.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (certificat d'inscription) of the SARL
Notarized articles of association
Manager's declaration regarding no AML convictions
Identification of all beneficial owners
Lease/domiciliation agreement for the registered office
Company bank account certificate (RIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT/CIT registration attracts penalties (0.5%–1% per month of delay); if the AEDT or CCSS queries the file, provide certified translations of the founding documents; a misclassification of the business as non-established must be corrected by filing the appropriate registration form within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commerce and operational clearances (establishment authorization check, e-commerce and physical logistics compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy — Direction générale des classes moyennes; municipal commune of the warehouse; Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM); Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify whether an 'autorisation d'établissement' (business establishment permit) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 is required for the planned warehouse/fulfilment facility; for pure online intermediation without a domestic shop, obtain written confirmation of exemption; if warehousing premises are leased, apply for municipal environmental/planning compatibility (commodo/incommodo) and CGDIS fire-safety certification; ensure ITM workplace compliance for manual handling and racking safety; appoint a data-protection representative if cross-border EU personal-data processing occurs.
required_dossiers: Copy of the RCS extract
Lease/title evidence for the warehouse or premises
Fire-safety certificate from CGDIS
Structural/electrical inspection certificates for the premises
Employee roster and work-schedule plan (if staff hired)
De minimis environmental declaration (if waste/storage thresholds apply)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment authorization is refused due to insufficient professional-competency evidence, submit diplomas and prior employment certificates ('états de service') and lodge an administrative appeal to the Minister of the Economy within 3 months; environmental/fire compliance deficits are cured by implementing corrective engineering measures and requesting a fresh inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy — Direction générale des classes moyennes (Small and Medium Enterprises Directorate); for physical premises additionally the municipal commune where the warehouse or fulfilment centre is located
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for pure online retail of oversized furniture and home decor (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 449110) without a domestic physical store; if a warehouse or fulfilment centre is operated in Luxembourg, an 'Autorisation d'établissement' under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 and a municipal environmental compatibility certificate (commodo/incommodo) may apply depending on premises size

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) within the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration tier — online retail and warehousing of finished furniture (no manufacturing, no coating, no VOC-emitting production) is not listed in the Grand-Ducal EIA annexes; a simplified 'commodo/incommodo' declaration is required only if warehouse floor area exceeds 2,000 m², or if more than 100 parking spaces or fuel storage installations are present
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If premises are operated: wastewater discharges must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 November 1999 and the amended Law of 19 December 2008 on water management (pH 6.5–9; suspended solids <30 mg/l; COD <125 mg/l when connecting to public sewer); packaging and waste furniture components must be consigned to an approved waste facility under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; no VOC or combustion-emission thresholds are triggered because no finishing or production occurs; if diesel-forklift equipment is used, comply with EU engine emission standards (Regulation (EU) 2016/1628) and national clean-air rules

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance certificate (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) for any commercial/warehouse premises at occupancy of 200 persons or floor area of 1,000 m²; structural load inspection certificate prepared by an agréé engineer for racking and shelving of oversized furniture per Eurocode standards; workplace safety clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering ergonomics of manual handling of oversized goods, rack anchoring, electrical systems and floor-load rating; where employees are engaged, compliance with the Labour Code (Code du travail) on first-aid equipment, fire drills and a written safety and health plan

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) / Registration portal: MyGuichet.lu (business registration via RCS and tax number application through the Luxembourg direct tax administration)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SARL must first file incorporation documents with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a notary; post-incorporation, the RCS automatically transmits corporate data to the Administration des contributions directes and the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), which issues the national tax number (numéro de registre national / matricule) and separate VAT number after submission of the VAT registration form (Formulaire 645) either via MyGuichet.lu or by post. Non-resident directors and shareholders may be appointed; no local residency requirement applies to initial registration, but a Luxembourg registered office and designated local agent (when no local director) are required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg SARL is subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax at entity level; no US-style check-the-box election exists. However, a fully taxable Luxembourg entity may form part of a corporate tax consolidation regime under Article 164bis LIR allowing integrated tax grouping among 95%-owned Luxembourg resident companies. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD implementation (Law of 27 December 2019) apply and may restrict deductions where payments are treated asymmetrically. Election for the Luxembourg VAT group regime is available per Article 59bis of the Luxembourg VAT Law for VAT purposes only.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for Luxembourg-established businesses: any taxable person making taxable supplies is required to register. For EU distance sales of goods (non-established suppliers), the VAT registration threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year (Union-wide distance sales threshold); below this, VAT may be due in the customer's member state. For non-EU established suppliers, mandatory registration arises with immediate effect upon any taxable supply unless the Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) is used for distance sales of imported consignments not exceeding EUR 150.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently imposes no mandatory electronic invoicing in B2B domestic supplies nor a real-time fiscal clearance/stamping mandate. E-invoicing is permitted, subject to authenticity and integrity requirements (suitable business controls or EDI under Directive 2006/112/EC). Luxembourg has implemented EU e-reporting optionality and anticipates the EU ViDA framework; from 1 July 2026, IOSS and OSS taxpayers must maintain e-invoicing-compliant record availability, but no national clearance API or mandatory clearance stamp applies to domestic e-commerce transactions at present.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Luxembourg supplier may apply 0% VAT to the export supply of goods if title passes within Luxembourg and goods are dispatched/transported outside the EU, or if the goods are shipped to another EU member state and the onward export is made by the customer or a third party under the VAT-exempt export provisions (Articles 155 and 156 of Luxembourg VAT Law). Documentation proving that the goods left Luxembourg/EU territory must be retained. For online retail of oversized furniture, zero-rating applies only to actual exports outside the EU; EU-distance sales remain taxable at the destination country's VAT rate, either via OSS registration or local VAT registration. Sales of offshore services (e.g., in-transit logistics, online marketplace facilitation) are zero-rated under Article 155(b) where the recipient is established outside the EU and direct effective use/exploitation occurs outside Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Accompanying Document – EAD) issued via LU Single Administrative Document / AES
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (CMR, Air Waybill, seaway bill)
Proof of export contract and purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange or bank settlement evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg tax administration and customs authorities may audit export zero-rating claims. If the exporter fails to provide valid dispatch/export proof or the goods are diverted back into the EU, VAT may be clawed back with interest at the statutory late-interest rate; the penalty regime includes fines up to 100% of evaded VAT for intentional fraud, administrative fines for material omissions, and potential criminal prosecution for forging customs declarations or false export documentation. Failure to repatriate foreign receipts within 180 days may trigger reclassification of the export as taxable domestic supply, VAT reassessment, and transfer-pricing adjustments where the exporter is a related entity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem framework alongside the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), with the Ministry of Finance holding residual authority over exchange-control policy. As a euro-area member, Luxembourg applies the full free movement of capital under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and maintains no separate exchange-control administration or licensing regime for current or capital account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts; Luxembourg law and applicable EU treaty provisions impose no conversion restrictions, no prior-authorisation mechanisms, no surrender requirements and no economic-benefit or investment-screening tests for foreign ownership of a SARL. Profit remittance by a SARL is unrestricted under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, subject only to (i) an annual general meeting approval, (ii) the statutory balance-sheet solvency test requiring net assets to remain at or above the issued share capital plus non-distributable reserves after distribution, and (iii) a standard 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, which may be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the domestic participation-exemption regime where the parent holds at least 10% and satisfies the holding-period condition; there are no capital controls, no reinvestment obligations and no profit-repatriation quotas. The only administrative hurdle in practice is the requirement that annual accounts be filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and that any shareholder loan be documented at arm's length for tax purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion rules apply. Luxembourg and the Eurosystem do not impose any statutory timeline or required conversion ratio for export proceeds, trade settlement receipts or inbound revenue from e-commerce payment aggregators; EUR and foreign-currency balances may be held indefinitely both onshore and offshore without declaration to the BCL. The sole relevant obligation is statistical: under the ECB external-sector statistics framework implemented by the BCL, resident enterprises are required to provide their bank with transaction and counterparty details for direct-investment and goods-trade flows equal to or exceeding EUR 12.5 million per counterparty per calendar year, and the bank then files the report on the company's behalf; this is a statistical-reporting duty, not an exchange-control, surrender or conversion requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué for notarial incorporation) and Operational Account with EUR/USD multicurrency sub-accounts
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account with EUR/USD multicurrency sub-accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility as an auxiliary settlement layer, not as the primary treasury home. CSSF-licensed Luxembourg electronic money institutions under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, and EEA EMIs passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2 (e.g., Stripe Payments Europe Limited, an Irish-authorised EMI, or Wise Europe / Revolut Payments UAB), can provide EUR/USD IBANs, faster remote onboarding and API-driven multi-currency accounts suited to receiving Stripe and Affirm BNPL payouts. Legal constraints: an EMI is not a credit institution, cannot grant credit, open documentary credits or issue import guarantees, and is prudentially subject to own-funds requirements equal to the greater of EUR 350,000 or 2% of outstanding e-money float, creating settlement-concentration risk for large trade disbursements; additionally, Tier-1 banks may treat major incoming flows from EMI pooled settlement accounts as heightened AML risk and may refuse to accept such funds as evidence of commercial substance. Recommended architecture: one Tier-1 bank account as the master clearing account and a single EMI used only for payout-optimisation sweeps, never the reverse.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law (Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended) and CSSF Regulation 12-02 require positive identification of all gérants and ultimate beneficial owners. Physical attendance at the bank branch is not a statutory precondition where eIDAS-compliant remote identification (video interview, OCR document verification and qualified electronic signature) is deployed, but in practice the Tier-1 universal banks require at least one physical interview with the managing director or, for non-resident directors, a notarised power of attorney with apostille plus a certified true copy of the passport; remote opening is generally permitted only under enhanced due diligence and may result in a 4-to-8-week onboarding delay and a six-month heightened-compliance cohort. The SARL incorporation itself mandates appearance before a Luxembourg notary, either in person or through a notarised power of attorney, and the bank will request the authenticated notarial deed and the RCS extract as standard documentation. Recommended approach: appoint a resident gérant who attends the initial bank meeting in person; non-resident shareholders execute an apostilled notarised POA, thereby reducing onboarding friction and avoiding rejection risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment-aggregator settlement: high-velocity micro-payments from Stripe and BNPL plans arriving in pooled settlement funds that obscure the identity of the underlying consumer payors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sign the merchant-services agreement with Stripe Payments Europe Limited and the BNPL provider; provide the six-month payout history with anonymised transaction IDs, fee schedules, batch-to-order reconciliation mapping, confirmed delivery documentation, refund and dispute ledgers, and evidence of automated ERP reconciliation; present the commercial logic of each settlement batch to the bank's financial-crime unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BNPL consumer-credit nexus: bank concern that the SARL is originating regulated consumer credit by offering instalment financing at checkout.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Demonstrate that the BNPL provider (Affirm or its licensed EEA financing partner) is the sole creditor under the Luxembourg Law of 14 July 2016 on consumer credit and that the SARL acts only as an unregulated merchant beneficiary; file the contractual merchant terms, the provider's regulatory licences, confirmation that no interest or credit charges are collected by the SARL, and the opt-out flow for consumers directed to the lender's portal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with opaque source of funds for the minimum share capital of EUR 12,394.68 (25% paid up at incorporation) and any subsequent shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised incorporation deed with apostille, certified passport or certificate of good standing of the shareholder, three months of pre-funding bank statements, evidence of lawful origin of wealth (salary, sale of assets or divestment proceeds), shareholder-loan agreement at arm's-length interest, and the bank's own capital-block certificate confirming the escrow arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening mismatch in a non-face-to-face cross-border model with unknown final consumers of oversized home furniture.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement an automated sanctions/PEP/financial-crime screening tool covering customers, suppliers, logistics carriers and freight forwarders; maintain full supply-chain documentation (Bills of Lading, CMR notes, packing lists, Incoterms 2020 contracts) evidencing physical goods flow and excluding embargoed or dual-use origin; align risk-tiering with CSSF guidance and OLAF recommendations and demonstrate quarterly screening logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback and refund ratio from oversized-furniture delivery disputes, triggering reclassification as high-risk distance-selling with prepayment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a structured dispute register with refunds executed within the statutory 14-day EU distance-selling withdrawal period, produce signed proof-of-delivery records and freight insurance certificates, implement PSD2-SCA-compliant 3D-Secure checkout through Stripe, cap the monthly refund ratio within bank-acceptable limits, and evidence the chargeback-reserve accounting policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for share capital and shareholder funding: (1) the non-resident shareholder executes a SWIFT MT103 credit in EUR to the SARL's blocked capital-escrow account at a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank, using ISO 20022 External Purpose Code CAPM (capital payment) or INTC (intra-company payment) and a structured field-70 reference reading 'Capital subscription - [SARL name] - notarial deed dated [date]'; (2) the bank issues the attestation de blocage de fonds to the notary, evidencing that EUR 12,394.68 (or higher stated capital) is blocked until registration; (3) after signature of the deed and RCS registration, the bank releases the escrow to the SARL's free operational IBAN; (4) any shareholder loan above EUR 15,000 must be supported by an arm's-length interest-bearing loan agreement, reported in the annual corporate tax return, and may require the bank to record the transaction for BCL external-statistics purposes if aggregate direct-investment flows reach EUR 12.5 million per counterparty per year; (5) repayment of principal and interest is unrestricted and requires no authorisation. The bank will verify that the CAPM/INTC purpose code matches the RCS capital figure and that the credit settles through TARGET2.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the oversized home-furniture trade cycle: (a) EU suppliers and warehouses: SEPA Credit Transfer (including instant SCT) in EUR, or SEPA Direct Debit for recurring freight and storage charges; (b) non-EU suppliers (chiefly China and Vietnam invoiced in USD or CNY): SWIFT MT103/MT202 for invoice settlement with ISO 20022 purpose code TRAD or GOODS, accompanied by the commercial invoice, packing list and transport documents; (c) large single consignments exceeding EUR 100,000: irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit under UCP 600 issued by the Tier-1 Luxembourg bank, payable at sight against presentation of Bill of Lading, invoice and insurance certificate; (d) import duties and freight: postponed VAT accounting under the Luxembourg import-VAT deferment so cash is not advanced for customs VAT, with freight forwarders paid via SEPA or MT103; (e) inbound e-commerce receivables: Stripe settles via its Irish EMI to the SARL's EUR IBAN through SEPA or in USD via SWIFT, with daily automated sweeps from any EMI sub-account to the master Tier-1 account to minimise counterparty float exposure. All outbound instructions must carry valid ISO 20022 purpose codes, and the bank may require the underlying contracts on file for any USD settlement above its AML threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla EUR/USD delivery forwards with tenors up to 12 months, executed with a Luxembourg credit institution under ISDA 2002 or a bilateral FX master agreement; the SARL qualifies as a non-financial counterparty (NFC) under EMIR and is not subject to mandatory clearing for such forwards.
FX swaps (swap de change) combining a spot and a forward EUR/USD or EUR/CNH leg to manage the timing mismatch between USD-denominated Stripe/Affirm settlements and EUR supplier payments.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR/USD) limited to matched asset-liability hedging of any USD-denominated shareholder loan, subject to confirmation of NFC- status and the absence of any EMIR clearing-threshold breach (EUR 3 billion gross notional).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) restricted to non-convertible or offshore-regulated currencies (e.g., USD/CNH) where onshore CNY delivery is unavailable; NDFs are not applicable to EUR/USD within the euro area.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SARL's managers to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and potential criminal fines up to EUR 125,000; repeated or continued failure can trigger Court of Commerce enforcement and, for habitual non-compliance, proceedings leading to administrative strike-off of the company from the RCSL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax / Municipal Business Tax Return (Declarations for CIT, Municipal Business Tax and Net Wealth Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due by 31 May of the year following the tax period; effective filing deadlines are shown on the official tax notice and may be extended on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing triggers automatic penalty assessments, default interest of 0.6% per month on outstanding tax, and administrative fines; deliberate non-filing may expose managers to criminal penalties under the Luxembourg General Tax Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Annual Confirmation Filing (Confirmations Annuelles des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) through the Luxembourg Business Registers platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Confirmation is mandatory during the first month of each calendar year, i.e., by 31 January, confirming that the beneficial ownership information on file remains accurate or reflecting any changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes a criminal offence; intentional breach may lead to imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years and/or fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 250,000; negligent failure carries lower but still substantial financial penalties, plus publication of the sanction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net Wealth Tax Return (Impôt sur la Fortune) and Minimum Net Wealth Tax Acknowledgement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Direct Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual corporate income tax return, normally by 31 May following the tax year; minimum net wealth tax band and annual instalment conditions apply to SARLs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers default interest at 0.6% per month, administrative fines, and recovery proceedings; persistent failure may be treated as a serious bookkeeping and filing breach exposing the entity to winding-up and strike-off procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of Registered Office and Corporate Details with the RCSL (Periodic Confirmation / Extrait Correction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not a separate fixed annual calendar event, but must be performed whenever data is amended and is verified at least annually during any corporate filing; companies using a registered agent must provide an annual address confirmation before the agent's renewal date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or outdated RCSL data is an administrative offence; RCSL may impose fines and, in cases of prolonged failure to maintain accurate disclosure, may initiate a judicial request for strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL is exempt from mandatory statutory audit if it does not exceed in two consecutive financial years two of the three following thresholds for small undertakings: balance sheet total of EUR 4,400,000, net turnover of EUR 8,800,000, and average workforce of 50 employees; mandatory audit by an approved independent auditor (Réviseur d'Entreprises) is required when those thresholds are exceeded, for public-interest entities, for companies whose parent or group is subject to consolidated audit, and when otherwise imposed by the articles of association, shareholders, or the Court
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual accounts must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) as codified in the Luxembourg Commercial Code, implementing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated financial statements and is optional for certain regulated or listed entities, not for a standard private SARL

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: By 31 January of each calendar year, every Luxembourg SARL must file through Luxembourg Business Registers an annual confirmation declaring that the beneficial ownership information recorded in the RBE is still accurate; when shareholding transfers or other ownership changes have occurred during the prior year, the SARL must simultaneously update the RBE with the new beneficial owners and file a revised ownership structure, ensuring the register necessarily shows immediate and indirect holdings equal to at least 25% plus one share or 25% ownership rights
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shareholders/Associates (Registre des Associés) kept at the registered office, including current shareholding, transfers, and ownership distribution
Minutes of General Meetings and written shareholder resolutions
Minutes of Board of Managers Resolutions/Management Decisions
Share Transfer Register and share subscription documentation (for SARLs with issued quotas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,800 - $4,500 per full year for a Luxembourg corporate services provider or registered office/trust company (including usual registered agent duties and RCSL correspondence handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit fee for a SARL below the legal size thresholds; when mandatory audit applies, a typical engagement for a mid-sized retail/warehouse entity ranges from $6,000 to $18,000 per financial year, depending on transaction volume, inventory complexity, and group reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Solidarity surcharge of 7% on IRC; municipal business tax (communal tax) varies by municipality (approx. 6.75%–11.2%); IP regime with 80% exemption on qualifying IP income; participation exemption for dividends and capital gains; notional interest deduction (NID) for equity financing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the eCDF portal (MyGuichet.lu)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; extensions may be granted upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only; apply DTA provisions if applicable.
Add back any non-deductible items per Luxembourg tax law.
Claim exemption if holding criteria met; attach supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credit, investment tax credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute credit per DTA or unilateral relief; provide TRC and proof of foreign tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 0.6% of tax due per month, capped at 10% of tax due; late payment interest: 0.6% per month; additional fines up to €25,000 for willful non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under participation exemption if shareholding ≥10% or acquisition price ≥€1.2 million, held for at least 12 months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit Form 105 (for dividends) or Form 106 (for interest/royalties) to the Luxembourg tax administration (ACD) before payment, accompanied by a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the recipient's jurisdiction. Alternatively, apply for a refund after payment within the statutory time limit (usually 5 years).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% (no WHT on interest except for profit-sharing loans); Royalties: 0% (no WHT on royalties, but anti-abuse rules may apply if paid to a related party in a low-tax jurisdiction). Treaty rates may apply if any.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Group consolidated turnover > €50 million AND local entity intercompany transactions > €1 million (services), > €250,000 (other transactions), or > €100,000 (financial transactions)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) for entities benefiting from certain regimes (e.g., IP box). For general trading companies, substance is required to avoid being classified as a shell; OECD BEPS and EU ATAD anti-abuse rules apply. The company must maintain adequate personnel, premises, and decision-making functions in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, falsification of books, or concealment of assets to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 200% of evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real economic substance (no employees, premises, or business activity) solely to obtain tax benefits or avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and imposition of 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions; fines up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if the company is deemed a sham; potential criminal charges for abuse of law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering (AML) procedures, including customer due diligence, record-keeping, and reporting of suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines and imprisonment if they knowingly facilitate money laundering; regulatory bans from holding directorial positions.
